subject: Order Form commercial terms: payment cadence, minimum commit guardrails & net-terms exception

Subject: Redwood Order Form — payment cadence and tax handling

Karthik —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement has circulated a draft PO (attached) and we have two asks before we can move to signatures: 1) GreenLab requests Net60 on the remainder of the contract after an initial invoice (we typically operate Net60 for mid-market vendors); and 2) we need clarity on how VAT/withholding will be handled for EU usage — whether Redwood will issue gross invoices or if GreenLab should withhold and provide tax certificates.

We are fine with a minimum commit schedule, but procurement will need clear invoicing cadence and an acceptance that billing entity is Redwood Inc. Can you share a short summary of the payment/cashflow options you can do and any potential adjustments to the Order Form payment lines? Attached: GreenLab_PO_20260601.pdf, GreenLab_tax_cert.pdf

Best,
Sarah Boone
Senior Procurement Manager
GreenLab Therapeutics

Subject: Re: Redwood Order Form — payment cadence and tax handling

Sarah —

Appreciate the clear ask and the PO — thanks. High level options from our side (we're trying to balance your cashflow needs with Redwood's predictable-revenue model):

- Standard: Net30 on receipt for all invoices. No prepay.
- Compromise A: 25% upfront (activation), 75% invoiced monthly Net30 with quarterly true-up vs usage.
- Compromise B (finance-friendly): 30% upfront, then remainder invoiced in two tranches (month 1 and month 3) with Net45 on each tranche.

On tax: Redwood issues gross invoices from Redwood Inc. where applicable. For EU customers we typically ask for VAT registration and withholding evidence; if withholding applies we net the withholding on our invoices and supply a certificate request flow. Kimberly — can you attach an Order Form with the redlines for the three options above and call out the tax evidence we need? Ben — please advise whether Finance can accept Net45 for the remainder without a financing fee and what guardrails we should include on minimum commits. Lauren — if we need legal signoff on a Net60 exception, can you flag the specific clause to surface in the MSA/Order Form?

Cc'ing our internal ops to speed turnaround.

Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-03T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood Order Form — payment cadence and tax handling

Team —

Finance perspective: Net30 is the default; Net45 is tolerable for the remainder after an upfront, but Net60 materially increases our DSO and exposure. If Procurement insists on Net60 we would ask for one of the following mitigations:

- Maintain 30% upfront and move the remainder to Net45 but add a 1.0% financing fee on outstanding balance beyond Net45; or
- Keep Net60 but add an escrow/letter-of-credit for the first two quarters capped at 20% of committed ARR; or
- Accept Net60 for the first year only if GreenLab provides a corporate guarantee or pre-approved credit check and remit a partial upfront (40%).

Minimum commit guardrail: we require a quarterly true-up and a clause that shortfalls below 75% of the committed tier trigger a reconciliation invoice or credit in the following quarter. That protects forecasted run-rate without being punitive.

I'll mark up an internal redline of the payment table and attach to Kimberly's doc.

Ben Carter
Director, Revenue Operations
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Redwood Order Form — payment cadence and tax handling

Sarah — attaching a redline of the Order Form that reflects: 1) a 30% activation/one-time invoice; 2) two split tranches for the remaining committed value with Net45 terms; 3) quarterly true-up language; and 4) tax appendix language requiring GreenLab to provide VAT registration and withholding certificates within 30 days of first invoice. Attachment: OrderForm_GLab_redline.docx

Key commercial notes in the redline:
- Payment schedule table (rows): Activation 30% (immediate), Tranche A 35% (invoice on Day 30, Net45), Tranche B 35% (invoice on Day 90, Net45).
- Shortfall / Minimum Commit: If actual usage <75% of committed during a quarter, Customer owes the difference in the next invoice period.
- Net60 exceptions: we have an optional clause (MSA Exhibit) to allow Net60 for the remainder of the term with either (a) 1.0% monthly financing fee, or (b) escrow covering 20% of committed ARR for first two quarters.
- Taxes: Customer is responsible for VAT/gross-up unless they provide acceptable withholding certificates; Redwood will reissue invoices if requested after verification.

Please let us know if GreenLab can accept the Net45 path with the 30% activation. If not, Karthik, I think we need procurement to confirm which of Ben's mitigations they'd consider.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Commercial Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the redline. Quick responses from Procurement/Finance side: GreenLab cannot provide 30% upfront on this engagement (budget profile). Our preferred path would be: 15% activation + Net60 on the remainder. If Redwood will not accept Net60 without mitigation, we can offer an alternate: 15% activation, remainder Net60 with a 0.5% monthly financing fee (applied after Net45), and we will provide VAT registration documentation and withholding certificates within 30 days.

We are not able to do escrow or a corporate guarantee at this time. If you can accept a small financing fee and lower activation, we can move quickly to DocuSign — I'll circulate an internal approval if Karthik confirms.

On invoicing entity: GreenLab prefers invoices issued to GreenLab Therapeutics, Inc. (US entity) with Redwood's tax info on file.

Sarah Boone
Senior Procurement Manager
GreenLab Therapeutics

Sarah / Marco —

Thanks — good, pragmatic trade. Can confirm Redwood will accept the following compromise to close the deal quickly:

- Commercial compromise: 15% activation invoice due on signature; remainder invoiced Net60.
- Mitigation: a 0.5% monthly financing fee applicable to any amount outstanding beyond Net45 (i.e., no fee if paid between Net31–Net45; fee starts Day 46).
- Additional guardrails: quarterly true-up; shortfall reconciliation if usage <75% of committed tier; Redwood reserves right to convert to Net45 on renewal if DSO > 75 days persist.
- Taxes: GreenLab to provide VAT registration + withholding certificates within 30 days; Redwood will accept gross invoicing and reissue as necessary upon evidence.
